history: Clandestino means ‘hidden’, and it goes back to Latin clam, ‘in secret’, with the ending of clandestinus, ‘done secretly’. Italian first used it for any activity that happens out of sight: una riunione clandestina, a secret meeting, or la stampa clandestina, the underground press of the Resistance. Later it became common for people who enter or stay in a country without permission, and un clandestino is still used in the news. Many institutions, associations and journalists now prefer to avoid it for a person, because it defines someone by a legal status. They say migrante irregolare or persona senza permesso di soggiorno instead. As a learner you will hear all of these. The Latin adjective belongs to the same family as celare, ‘to hide’.
